subject: Service reachability interruption — mitigation steps & verification
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Analytics <ops@acme-analytics.com>, Kira Tanaka <kira@seamlessretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service reachability interruption — mitigation steps & verification

Hi Sam / Kira —

Quick note from the ops desk: our monitoring shows degraded egress to EU and APAC zones via a third‑party cloud peering provider starting ~08:45 UTC. This is impacting a subset of customer requests routed through region-prefixed endpoints and is causing elevated latencies and some 5xxs for tenants with EU/APAC affinity.

Immediate mitigations we recommend (low-friction options you can try now):

- Switch to the global-fallback endpoint for the duration of the event: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/global-fallback (no config changes to keys). This will route to our multi-region bridge and reduce tail latency.
- If you use region query params, set region=us for short-term traffic (example: region=us-west).
- Reduce request concurrency briefly (client-side throttle) if you see token errors to avoid queueing spikes.

Attached is a short checklist (reroute-checklist-v1.pdf) with curl examples and DNS glide instructions.

What we need from you: please confirm which of the two options above you can apply now (global-fallback or region param) and note any constraints (e.g., data-residency rules). Once you confirm, we will validate from our side and monitor.

I'll keep you posted with updates from engineering. Apologies for the disruption — we know this can be painful during high-traffic windows.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

From: ops@acme-analytics.com
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Sep 2028 09:27:14 -0400
Subject: Re: Service reachability interruption — mitigation steps & verification

Thanks Jonas —

We can switch to the global-fallback endpoint immediately. One question: will switching change which model or version is served (we rely on a pinned model for some regulated workloads)? Also, will requests routed to global-fallback still be logged to our tenant audit logs in the same retention window?

We will perform the switch within the next 10 minutes and report back.

— Sam (ops@acme-analytics.com)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Analytics <ops@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Sep 2028 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service reachability interruption — mitigation steps & verification

Sam — thanks, appreciate the quick response. Short answers:

- Model/version: the global-fallback routes to the same model family and honors model pinning where possible. If we need an exact model binary (customer-managed pin), confirm and we'll route you to a compatible host.
- Audit logs: all requests continue to be recorded to tenant audit logs and retained per your account settings. No change to retention during the bridge.

Ben / Neha — looping you in to confirm we can 1) validate model pinning for Acme and 2) watch audit-event continuity while they make the switch. Ben, can your team run a quick validation sweep once Sam confirms? Neha, if engineering has a short hotfix or routing override we should apply, please advise.

On Tue, Sep 4, 2028 at 09:27, ops@acme-analytics.com wrote:
> Thanks Jonas —
> 
> We can switch to the global-fallback endpoint immediately...

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Sep 2028 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Service reachability interruption — mitigation steps & verification (post-incident details)

Team — postmortem summary and next steps (short):

Root cause: an unannounced maintenance window by our peering partner eliminated a subset of advertised routes into EU & APAC for ~45 minutes. Traffic for region-prefixed endpoints attempted the impacted paths and hit elevated error rates.

What we did in the window:
- Opened emergency BGP sessions and pushed routing overrides to route traffic via our multi-region bridge.
- Issued the global-fallback endpoint recommendation to customers.
- Applied temporary rate-limits on inbound traffic to avoid overload on bridge hosts.

Customer impact: increased 5xxs and latency for EU/APAC-affine requests between 08:45–09:30 UTC. Affected tenants: Acme Analytics, Seamless Retail (partial). We validated that requests routed via global-fallback served the pinned model family and audit logs remained intact.

Follow-ups (action items):
1) Engineering to add automated failover policies to detect similar BGP anomalies and auto-flip to bridge within 60s (owner: neha.kapoor).
2) Networking team to add secondary peering peer and contractual SLA with provider (owner: ben.carter).
3) Product to expose explicit endpoint guidance in the Console (owner: lauren.bishop).
4) CS/AM check-ins with affected customers and confirm they have no outstanding compliance concerns (owner: jonas.weber).

Attachments: postmortem-acme-20280906.pdf (detailed timeline, packet captures redacted).

I'll publish the public incident note to the status page once legal signs off on wording.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Analytics <ops@acme-analytics.com>, Kira Tanaka <kira@seamlessretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 Sep 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident: verification complete and next steps

Hi Sam / Kira —

Thanks again for working with us during the event. Quick recap and what to expect next: 

- Status: the peering issue has been resolved by the provider; our bridge and route overrides have been removed. We validated that requests after 12:00 UTC flow normally.
- Verification: our team confirmed model pinning continuity and audit-log retention for your tenant during the switch. If you see any gaps in telemetry, reply with example request-ids and we will investigate.
- Credits: as a courtesy we will apply a one-time service credit for request errors during the incident window. I will send a separate billing note once the credit is applied.

Attached: postmortem-acme-20280906.pdf (redacted technical timeline) and the reroute checklist. Public incident page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2028-09-04

Action for you: if you have strict data-residency requirements that prevent using global-fallback in future events, let me know and we will schedule a scoped routing playbook and a runbook run with your security team.

We value your trust — I'll be available if you want a 1:1 review of the timeline.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
